title: Aflrpn4 Represents a Promising Target for Mitigating Aspergillus flavus Growth and Aflatoxin Contamination.
authors: Liu, Xingsai; Xin, Yanli; Sahibzada, Kashif Iqbal; Zhang, Xiujia; Tu, Cunjian; Wei, Shan; Hu, Yuansen; Lv, Yangyong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄曲霉转录因子Aflrpn4的基因功能，纯湿实验表型与代谢分析，无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Aspergillus flavus and its primary secondary metabolite, aflatoxin B1, pose a persistent threat to global food security and public health, highlighting the need to identify novel molecular targets for the development of highly specific fungicides. In this study, the transcription factor Aflrpn4 was investigated by constructing gene deletion and complementation strains to elucidate its regulatory mechanisms in controlling the growth, development, and pathogenicity of A. flavus. Phenotypic analysis revealed that, compared with the wild-type and complemented strains, loss of Aflrpn4 severely restricted radial colony growth, reduced conidial yield, and caused structural defects in conidiophores. Furthermore, AFB1 content was reduced by 52% compared with the wild-type. In storage simulation assays using peanut and maize kernels, the DeltaAflrpn4 strain exhibited significantly compromised colonization capacity, reduced biomass, and lower AFB1 accumulation. Under aflatoxin-inducing YES culture conditions, deletion of Aflrpn4 was associated with significant downregulation of key pathway-specific regulatory and structural genes, including aflR, aflS, and aflP. Furthermore, under osmotic stress induced by 1.2 M NaCl and KCl, the growth inhibition rates of the DeltaAflrpn4 strain reached 70% and 59%, respectively, and cell membrane integrity was severely compromised. Loss of Aflrpn4 also disrupted intracellular redox homeostasis, characterized by a significant decrease in superoxide dismutase activity, compensatory increases in catalase and peroxidase activities, and substantial accumulation of reactive oxygen species. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Aflrpn4 acts as a pivotal regulator coordinating vegetative growth, asexual development, stress adaptation, and aflatoxin biosynthesis in A. flavus. Consequently, Aflrpn4 represents a promising molecular target for developing targeted interventions to control A. flavus and aflatoxin contamination during grain storage.
abstract_zh: 黄曲霉（Aspergillus flavus）及其主要次生代谢产物黄曲霉毒素B1对全球粮食安全和公共卫生构成持续威胁，凸显了识别新型分子靶点以开发高特异性杀菌剂的必要性。本研究通过构建基因缺失和互补菌株，对转录因子Aflrpn4进行了研究，以阐明其在调控黄曲霉生长、发育和致病性中的调节机制。表型分析显示，与野生型和互补菌株相比，Aflrpn4的缺失严重限制了菌落径向生长，降低了分生孢子产量，并导致分生孢子梗结构缺陷。此外，与野生型相比，AFB1含量降低了52%。在使用花生和玉米籽粒的储存模拟试验中，DeltaAflrpn4菌株表现出显著受损的定殖能力、减少的生物量和较低的AFB1积累。在黄曲霉毒素诱导的YES培养条件下，Aflrpn4的缺失与关键途径特异性调控和结构基因（包括aflR、aflS和aflP）的显著下调相关。此外，在1.2 M NaCl和KCl诱导的渗透胁迫下，DeltaAflrpn4菌株的生长抑制率分别达到70%和59%，且细胞膜完整性严重受损。Aflrpn4的缺失还破坏了细胞内氧化还原稳态，其特征为超氧化物歧化酶活性显著降低、过氧化氢酶和过氧化物酶活性代偿性增加，以及活性氧的大量积累。综合这些发现表明，Aflrpn4作为关键调控因子，协调黄曲霉的营养生长、无性发育、胁迫适应和黄曲霉毒素生物合成。因此，Aflrpn4代表了开发靶向干预措施以控制谷物储存期间黄曲霉和黄曲霉毒素污染的潜在分子靶点。
